entries.name: isZero
doc: Whether all bits in the vector are zero.

entries.name: length
doc: Total number of addressable bits in the vector.

entries.name: popCount
doc: Total count of set bits (1s) across the entire vector.

entries.name: set
doc: Sets the bit at the given index to value.

entries.name: toBits
doc: Converts the bit-vector to an array of booleans.

entries.name: bitCount
doc: Total number of bits allocated.

entries.name: BloomFilter
doc: An immutable space-efficient probabilistic set filter.

entries.name: contains
doc: Tests if a string item may be present in the filter.

entries.name: containsBytes
doc: Tests if raw bytes may be present in the filter.

entries.name: create
doc: Constructs a raw BloomFilter with specified bit capacity and hash function count.

entries.name: estimatedCount
doc: Approximates the number of distinct items inserted.

entries.name: hashCount
doc: Number of independent hash functions used per item.

entries.name: insert
doc: Inserts a string item into the filter.

entries.name: insertBytes
doc: Inserts raw bytes into the filter.

entries.name: intersect
doc: Intersects two compatible filters via bitwise AND.

entries.name: merge
doc: Merges two compatible filters via bitwise OR.

entries.name: optimal
doc: Constructs an optimal BloomFilter for expected items and target false-positive probability.

entries.name: all
doc: Whether every value is true. True for an empty array.

entries.name: and
doc: Whether both are true. Both are evaluated, unlike `&&`, which is why this
exists: it can be passed as a function where the operator cannot.

entries.name: any
doc: Whether any value is true. False for an empty array.

entries.name: implies
doc: Whether the first being true forces the second to be.

entries.name: not
doc: The opposite of a truth value.

entries.name: or
doc: Whether either is true.

entries.name: select
doc: One of two values, chosen by a condition.
The false case comes first so the arguments read in the order `if` writes
its branches once the condition has been read.

entries.name: toInt
doc: A truth value as a whole number: one for true, nought for false.

entries.name: toText
doc: A truth value written out.

entries.name: xor
doc: Whether exactly one is true.

entries.name: alloc
doc: Allocates a new contiguous buffer of `bytes` length initialized to zero.

entries.name: Buffer
doc: A contiguous, unboxed sequence of raw bytes.
Backed directly by cache-aligned primitive byte storage without per-element
boxing. All scalar read, write, and scan operations are bounds-checked.

entries.name: compare
doc: Compares `len` bytes between buffer `a` at `aOff` and buffer `b` at `bOff`.
Follows standard lexicographical ordering (memcmp semantics):
- Returns `Some(0)` if both byte sequences are identical.
- Returns `Some(-1)` if the slice in `a` is lexicographically less than `b`.
- Returns `Some(1)` if the slice in `a` is lexicographically greater than `b`.
- Returns `None` if either range exceeds its respective buffer bounds.

entries.name: copy
doc: Copies `len` bytes from `src` at `srcOff` into `dst` at `dstOff`.
Returns the updated destination buffer, or `None` if any offset or length
violates memory boundaries.

entries.name: fill
doc: Fills `len` consecutive bytes starting at `offset` with `byte`.
Dispatches directly to contiguous memory block initialization (memset semantics).
Returns an updated buffer snapshot, or `None` if the fill range exceeds buffer bounds.

entries.name: fromBytes
doc: Wraps an existing `Bytes` sequence into a `Buffer`.

entries.name: readF64
doc: Reads a 64-bit IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point number at `offset` in little-endian order.
Utilizes hardware bit-casting with zero software decoding overhead.
Returns `None` if `offset` or `offset + 8` exceeds buffer bounds.

entries.name: readI64
doc: Reads a signed 64-bit integer at the given byte `offset` in little-endian two's-complement representation.
Returns `None` if `offset` or `offset + 8` exceeds buffer bounds.

entries.name: readU32
doc: Reads an unsigned 32-bit integer at `offset` in little-endian order.
Returns `None` if `offset` or `offset + 4` exceeds buffer bounds.

entries.name: readU64
doc: Reads an unsigned 64-bit integer at the given byte `offset` in little-endian order.
Returns `None` if `offset` or `offset + 8` exceeds buffer bounds.

entries.name: scanU64
doc: Scans up to `count` 64-bit words starting at `offset` for `needle`.
Returns the 0-based word index if found, or `None` if the value is not present
or the range exceeds buffer boundaries.

entries.name: size
doc: The length of the buffer in bytes.

entries.name: toBytes
doc: Exposes the underlying raw `Bytes` representation of the buffer.

entries.name: writeF64
doc: Writes a 64-bit IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point number at `offset` in little-endian order.
Utilizes hardware bit-casting directly into machine register representation.
Returns an updated buffer snapshot, or `None` if the write spans beyond buffer capacity.

entries.name: writeI64
doc: Writes a signed 64-bit integer at the given byte `offset` in little-endian two's-complement representation.
Returns an updated buffer snapshot, or `None` if the write spans beyond buffer capacity.

entries.name: writeU32
doc: Writes an unsigned 32-bit integer at `offset` in little-endian order.
Returns an updated buffer snapshot, or `None` if the write spans beyond buffer capacity.

entries.name: writeU64
doc: Writes an unsigned 64-bit integer at the given byte `offset` in little-endian order.
Returns an updated buffer snapshot, or `None` if the write spans beyond buffer capacity.

entries.name: bswap16
doc: Reverses the bytes of a 16-bit unsigned integer.

entries.name: bswap32
doc: Reverses the bytes of a 32-bit unsigned integer.

entries.name: bswap64
doc: Reverses the bytes of a 64-bit unsigned integer.

doc: Converts a 32-bit host integer to network byte order (Big-Endian).

entries.name: htons

doc: Converts a 32-bit network byte order integer to host byte order.

entries.name: ntohs

doc: Reads a 32-bit big-endian unsigned integer from `bytes` at `offset`.

doc: Serializes a 32-bit word into 4 big-endian bytes.

doc: Serializes a 64-bit word into 8 big-endian bytes.

entries.name: BytesError
doc: What went wrong while reading a byte sequence.
One variant per cause a caller can act on differently: a frame that ended
early is retried when more input arrives, while one holding a digit no
alphabet has is rejected outright, and a caller that could not tell them
apart could recover from neither.

entries.name: concat
doc: Two sequences joined. This copies, and is named so a reader can see it.

entries.name: contains

entries.name: decodeBase64

doc: The bytes URL-alphabet base64 spells, padded or not.

entries.name: decodeHex
doc: The bytes hexadecimal text spells, or why it spells none.
An odd number of digits is a length error rather than a digit error: the
digits may all be valid and the text still not name a whole number of bytes.

entries.name: drop
doc: Everything after the first bytes, sharing storage with the source.

entries.name: empty
doc: A sequence holding nothing.

entries.name: encodeBase64
doc: A sequence written as base64, padded to a multiple of four characters.

entries.name: encodeBase64Url

Padding is dropped because `=` is itself a character a URL escapes, which
is the whole reason this alphabet exists.

entries.name: encodeHex
doc: A sequence written as lower-case hexadecimal, two digits a byte.

entries.name: endsWith
doc: Whether a sequence ends with another.

entries.name: fromArray
doc: The bytes of an array of octets.

entries.name: fromText

entries.name: getText

doc: Read an unsigned integer in the byte order named by the function.

entries.name: u16Le
doc: The next two bytes as an unsigned number, least significant first.

entries.name: u32Be
doc: The next four bytes as an unsigned number, most significant first.

entries.name: u32Le
doc: The next four bytes as an unsigned number, least significant first.

entries.name: u64Be
doc: The next eight bytes as an unsigned number, most significant first.

entries.name: u64Le
doc: The next eight bytes as an unsigned number, least significant first.

entries.name: u8
doc: Read one octet without converting it through text.

entries.name: channel
doc: A channel holding at most the given count of items.
The bound is what makes a channel apply back-pressure: a sender waits when
the channel is full, so a fast producer is slowed to the speed of its
consumer rather than turning the difference into memory. A queue without a
bound does not remove that problem, it postpones it until there is no
memory left.
A bound below one is taken as one. A channel with no room could never be
sent to, and a caller writing zero meant the smallest useful channel rather
than one that stops the program.

entries.name: Channel
doc: A queue with a bound, carrying values of one type between threads.
The type parameter is carried by the channel rather than by what it holds,
so a channel of numbers and a channel of text are different types and
sending the wrong thing is a compile error. The token underneath is
untyped, which is why the type is kept here: it is the only place that can
hold it.

entries.name: ChannelError
doc: Why a channel operation did not do what it was asked.

entries.name: close
doc: Say that nothing more will be sent, so every receiver's loop can end.

entries.name: drain
doc: Every value still to come, in the order it was sent.
Named so its cost is visible: this holds every value at once, and `fold` is
the one that does not.

entries.name: fold
entries.signature: &Std.Channel.Channel[T] -> A -> fn(A, T) -> A -> Result[A, Std.Channel.ChannelError]
doc: Take values until the channel closes, combining them into one value.
The value is threaded rather than gathered by the step function, because a
function literal carries a copy of what it captured: a step assigning to a
variable outside itself would leave that variable as it found it.

entries.name: pending
doc: How many values are waiting.
A number that was true when it was read and may not be by the time it is
used, because another thread may send or receive in between. Right for a
report and wrong as a reason to skip a wait.

entries.name: receive
doc: Take the next value, waiting while the channel is empty.
Nothing means the channel is closed and empty, which is what ends a
receiver's loop. A closed channel still hands out what it already holds:
closing says nothing more will arrive, not that what arrived is discarded.

entries.name: send
doc: Put a value in, waiting while the channel is full.
Sending to a closed channel is refused rather than dropped. A producer
whose values were being discarded would have no way to find out, and that
is the failure most worth reporting.

entries.name: equalsIgnoreCase
doc: Whether two characters are the same ignoring ASCII case.

entries.name: fromCode
doc: The character with a given scalar value, or `None` when there is none.
Re-exported from the prelude so a caller reaching for character conversion
finds it beside everything else about characters.

entries.name: fromDigit
doc: The digit character for a value from 0 to 9, or `None` for anything else.

entries.name: isAlphanumeric
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII letter or decimal digit.

entries.name: isAscii
doc: Whether a character is in the ASCII range at all.
Everything else in this module answers about ASCII, so this is how a caller
learns whether the answers apply.

entries.name: isAsciiLower
doc: Whether a character is a lower-case ASCII letter.

entries.name: isAsciiUpper
doc: Whether a character is an upper-case ASCII letter.

entries.name: isControl
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII control character.

entries.name: isDigit
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII decimal digit.

entries.name: isHexDigit
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII hexadecimal digit.

entries.name: isIdentifier
doc: Whether a character is one a program may use in an identifier: a letter, a
digit, or an underscore.

entries.name: isLatin1
doc: Whether a character is in the Latin-1 range.

entries.name: isLetter
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII letter.

entries.name: isLower
doc: Whether an ASCII letter is lower case. A non-letter is not.

entries.name: isNumber
doc: Whether a character is a decimal digit, which is the only kind of number
this module recognises.

entries.name: isOctDigit
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII octal digit.

entries.name: isPrintable
doc: Whether a character is a printable ASCII character.

entries.name: isPunctuation
doc: Whether a character is an ASCII punctuation mark.

entries.name: isSeparator
doc: Whether a character is a space or a separator.

entries.name: isSymbol
doc: Whether a character is one of the ASCII symbols used in arithmetic and
comparison: the set a reader means by "an operator character".

entries.name: isUpper
doc: Whether an ASCII letter is upper case. A non-letter is not.

entries.name: isWhitespace
doc: Whether a character is a space, tab, carriage return, or newline.
The set is the ASCII one: recognising every Unicode space needs a table the
compiler does not yet carry, and claiming to without one would be worse than
saying so.

entries.name: ord
doc: A character's scalar value, named for what it is.

entries.name: toDigit
doc: The decimal value of a digit, or `None` for anything else.

entries.name: toHexDigit
doc: The value of a hexadecimal digit, or `None` for anything else.

entries.name: toLower
doc: The lower-case form of an ASCII letter; anything else is unchanged.

entries.name: toText
doc: A character as text, named for what it is.

entries.name: toTitle
doc: The title-case form of a character, which for ASCII is its upper case.

entries.name: toUpper
doc: The upper-case form of an ASCII letter; anything else is unchanged.

entries.name: addF64
doc: Vectorized element-wise addition of two float columns.
Produces a new float column containing the sum for each row where both inputs are non-null.

entries.name: appendF64
doc: Appends a valid 64-bit float scalar to the column.

entries.name: appendNullF64
doc: Appends a null row to the float column.

entries.name: appendNullU64
doc: Appends a null row to the column.
Leaves the validity bit as 0 and zeroes the underlying data slot.

entries.name: appendU64
doc: Appends a valid unsigned 64-bit scalar to the column.
Sets the validity bit to valid (1) and writes the scalar into contiguous unboxed storage.

entries.name: binarySearch
doc: Performs an O(log N) binary search over the valid portion of a sorted column.
Returns the matched row offset if found, or None if target is absent.

entries.name: binarySearchF64
doc: Performs an O(log N) binary search over the valid portion of a sorted float column.

entries.name: bitmapAnd
doc: Computes the bitwise AND of two row selection bitmaps.

entries.name: bitmapCount
doc: Counts the number of active matching rows set in the selection bitmap.

entries.name: bitmapNot
doc: Inverts the selection bitmap up to `rowCount` bits.

entries.name: bitmapOr
doc: Computes the bitwise OR of two row selection bitmaps.

entries.name: ColumnF64
doc: Contiguous unboxed 64-bit floating-point columnar vector.
Stores IEEE-754 double precision floats in contiguous unboxed buffer memory
alongside a null validity bitmap for SIMD-accelerated analytical processing.

entries.name: ColumnU64
doc: Contiguous unboxed 64-bit columnar vector.
Combines an unboxed scalar data buffer with a bit-packed null bitmap
for analytical vector processing and database scans.

entries.name: createF64
doc: Allocates an empty 64-bit float column with preallocated capacity.

entries.name: createU64
doc: Allocates an empty 64-bit unsigned integer column with preallocated capacity.

entries.name: filterGt
doc: Evaluates the predicate `(value > threshold)` on valid rows, producing a packed selection bitmap buffer.

entries.name: filterGtF64
doc: Evaluates the predicate `(value > threshold)` on valid float rows, producing a packed selection bitmap buffer.

entries.name: filterLtF64
doc: Evaluates the predicate `(value < threshold)` on valid float rows, producing a packed selection bitmap buffer.

entries.name: gather
doc: Gathers row elements according to a permutation index buffer into a new contiguous unboxed column.

entries.name: gatherF64
doc: Gathers float row elements according to a permutation index buffer into a new contiguous unboxed column.

entries.name: getF64
doc: Retrieves the float scalar at `row`, returning `None` if the row is null or out of bounds.

entries.name: getU64
doc: Retrieves the scalar at `row`, returning `None` if the row is null or out of bounds.

entries.name: isNull
doc: Checks whether the row at `row` is null or out of bounds.

entries.name: isNullF64
doc: Checks whether the float row at `row` is null or out of bounds.

entries.name: length
doc: Returns the number of rows stored in the column.

entries.name: lengthF64
doc: Returns the number of rows stored in the float column.

entries.name: max
doc: Computes the maximum value among valid non-null elements in the column.
Returns `None` if the column contains zero valid elements.

entries.name: maxF64
doc: Computes the maximum value among valid non-null elements in the float column.

entries.name: min
doc: Computes the minimum value among valid non-null elements in the column.
Returns `None` if the column contains zero valid elements.

entries.name: minF64
doc: Computes the minimum value among valid non-null elements in the float column.

entries.name: nullCount
doc: Returns the number of null values in the column.

entries.name: nullCountF64
doc: Returns the number of null values in the float column.

entries.name: project
doc: Gathers selected rows according to `selection` bitmap into a new contiguous unboxed column.

entries.name: projectF64
doc: Gathers selected float rows according to `selection` bitmap into a new contiguous unboxed column.

entries.name: sortIndices
doc: Computes an unboxed permutation index buffer containing row offsets sorted in ascending order.
Null rows are cleanly partitioned to the end of the permutation array (ASC NULLS LAST).

entries.name: sortIndicesF64
doc: Computes an unboxed permutation index buffer for float rows sorted in ascending order (ASC NULLS LAST).

entries.name: sum
doc: Computes the vectorized sum of all valid non-null elements in the column.

entries.name: sumF64
doc: Computes the vectorized sum of all valid non-null elements in the float column.

entries.name: compress
doc: Compatibility convenience for callers treating compression failure as fatal.

entries.name: compressChecked
doc: Compress bytes using the configured zlib level; checked form exposes host failure.

entries.name: CompressionLevel
doc: Compression optimization profile.

entries.name: compressText
doc: Compresses UTF-8 text into an RFC 1952 GZIP stream.

entries.name: config
doc: Constructs a default GZIP compression configuration.

entries.name: Configuring
doc: A configuration with one setting changed, each answering the configuration
rather than taking it apart.
Methods, so a configuration that differs from the default in two ways reads
down the page rather than wrapping each call in the next.

entries.name: crc32
doc: Calculates the standard IEEE 802.3 32-bit Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC-32) over input bytes.

entries.name: decompress
doc: Decode one gzip member with a default 64 MiB decompressed output limit.

entries.name: decompressText
doc: Decompresses an RFC 1952 GZIP stream and decodes the payload as UTF-8 text.

entries.name: decompressWithin
doc: Enforce output admission during inflation, including highly compressible inputs.

entries.name: GzipConfig
doc: Configuration parameters for streaming GZIP compression and HTTP middleware.

entries.name: GzipError
doc: Structured failure conditions encountered during GZIP stream decompression.

entries.name: middleware
doc: Compress eligible public responses without changing binary payload bytes on the wire.

entries.name: ConcurrentError
doc: Why a thread could not be started, or what it said when it failed.

entries.name: forEachBounded
doc: Apply an action to values with bounded concurrency, without implicit retries.

entries.name: join
doc: Wait for a thread to finish, and report what it said if it failed.
Joining twice answers the same way both times, so a scope joining its
children and a caller that already joined one do not race.

entries.name: joinAll
doc: Wait for every thread, in the order they were started.
The order is what makes a failure among them predictable: with several
threads failing, the one reported is the one started first rather than
whichever happened to finish first. A caller reading a report should not
have to run the program twice to see the same answer.

entries.name: mapBounded
doc: Map values with bounded concurrency, preserving input order and typed failures.

entries.name: mapResultBounded
entries.signature: &Array[T] -> Int -> fn(T) -> Result[U, E] -> Result[Result[Array[U], E], Std.Concurrent.ConcurrentError]
doc: Apply a fallible transform with bounded concurrency, returning the first error in input order.

entries.name: parallel
doc: Run every action at once and wait for all of them.
Every thread is started before any is joined. Starting and joining one at a
time would run them in sequence while looking like it did not, which is the
mistake this exists to make impossible to write by accident.

entries.name: parallelBounded
doc: Run a batch with bounded workers; each action is claimed at most once.

entries.name: sleep
doc: Wait, without holding the machine while waiting.

entries.name: start
doc: Start an action on a thread of its own.
The action is given the environment as it stands at the call, which is the
same environment an ordinary call would run in. Sharing it is safe because
every value in it is immutable: the things two threads can both change are
a channel, a lock, and a cell, and each of those is reached through
`Std.Channel` or `Std.Sync` rather than by writing to a variable.
A thread that failed does not take the program down. It reports what it
said to whoever joins it, which is the same rule every other operation
that reaches outside the program follows: the caller decides.

entries.name: Task
doc: A thread the program started.

entries.name: derive
doc: A key derived from a password, slowly and on purpose.
Slowness is the property: a password is short enough to guess, and this is
what makes each guess cost the guesser what it cost the owner once. The
iteration count is therefore not a tuning knob to lower — raise it as
machines get faster. See `Std.App.Password` for storing one.

entries.name: Digest
doc: A SHA-256 digest: eight words, which is the form the algorithm produces.
Kept as words rather than as text so a caller comparing two digests compares
numbers, and only rendering turns them into hexadecimal.

entries.name: digestsMatch
doc: Whether two digests are the same, compared in constant time.
Every word is examined whichever way the answer goes, so how long the
comparison took says nothing about where the two differed. A plain
comparison that stopped at the first difference would say exactly that, and
that is how a secret is guessed one byte at a time.

entries.name: hmacSha256
doc: The keyed digest that proves who a message came from.
A digest says a message was not altered by accident. A keyed digest says it
came from someone holding the key, which is the question a webhook, a
signed cookie, and an API signature all ask. Anyone can compute a digest of
a forged message; only a holder of the key can compute this.
This is where the compiler's own implementation is reached rather than the
one written above in Pudu. The reason is speed: a key derivation runs
thousands of these, and the readable implementation is for reading.

entries.name: hmacSha256Text
doc: The same, over text taken as UTF-8.

entries.name: keyLength
doc: How long a key for `seal` must be, in bytes.

entries.name: legacyBytes
doc: A legacy digest as the bytes it is, for a protocol that encodes them.

entries.name: LegacyDigest
doc: A SHA-1 digest: five words, which is the form that algorithm produces.
Present for the handshakes that specify it and for nothing else. It is not
a choice for anything that has to resist an adversary — collisions in it
have been produced — and it is separate from `Digest` so a caller cannot
pass one where the other belongs.

entries.name: legacyHex
doc: A legacy digest written as lower-case hexadecimal.

entries.name: nonceLength
doc: How long a nonce for `seal` must be, in bytes.

entries.name: open
doc: Open a sealed message, or answer nothing.
Nothing is answered for every reason a message might not be genuine — the
wrong key, a changed byte, a truncated message, associated data that does
not match. They are not told apart on purpose: saying which one failed
tells whoever changed the message which change got closer.

entries.name: seal
doc: Encrypt a message so that changing it is detected.
Encryption alone hides a message and says nothing about whether it arrived
as it was sent. Someone who cannot read a message can still change it, and
a program that decrypts whatever it is handed will act on the result. This
answers a sealed message whose tag covers both the encrypted part and the
`associated` part beside it — a record identifier, a version, a purpose —
which is how context that must travel in the clear is still protected from
being swapped.
The nonce must never be used twice with one key. Reusing one does not
merely weaken this, it reveals the messages, so derive a nonce or count
one; never reuse a fixed value.
Answers nothing when the key or nonce is the wrong length, which is a
mistake in the program rather than a fact about the message.

entries.name: secretsMatch
doc: Whether two texts are the same, compared in constant time.
For comparing a token a caller was given against one it holds, where the
time an ordinary comparison takes would leak how much of it was right.

entries.name: sha1
doc: The SHA-1 digest of text, taken over its UTF-8 bytes.
Where a protocol names this algorithm, the digest is proving that a party
followed the protocol rather than that it knows a secret, so what matters
is agreeing with every other implementation.

entries.name: sha1Bytes
doc: The SHA-1 digest of bytes.

entries.name: sha256
doc: The SHA-256 digest of text, taken over its UTF-8 bytes.

entries.name: sha256Bytes
doc: The SHA-256 digest of bytes.

entries.name: sha256Hex
doc: The SHA-256 of text, rendered as hexadecimal in one step.

entries.name: sha512
doc: The SHA-512 digest of bytes.
Beside SHA-256 rather than instead of it. A protocol names the digest it is
defined over — a signature algorithm, a key derivation, a transcript hash —
and substituting the one to hand produces a value that is not the one the
other side will compute.

entries.name: toHex
doc: A digest written as lower-case hexadecimal, which is how one is quoted.

entries.name: utf8
doc: Text as UTF-8 bytes.
Written here rather than taken from the runtime because it is bit work the
language can express, and a standard library that reached past the language
for it would be saying the language could not do it.

entries.name: column
doc: Every value in one column, or nothing when the table has no such column.

entries.name: CsvError
doc: Why text does not name a table.
A field opened with a quote and never closed is the one failure a reader
cannot recover from by guessing, because everything after it is inside the
field as far as the format is concerned.

entries.name: indexOfColumn
doc: Where a column sits, or `-1` when the table has no column of that name.

entries.name: parse
doc: Every row of a comma-separated text, fields already unquoted.
A row's fields are not counted against any other row's. A file whose rows
disagree is still read, because a reader that refused it would leave a
caller no way to see what was wrong; `parseTable` is where the count starts
to matter, because a name per column is a promise about every row.

entries.name: parseTable
doc: A table whose first row names its columns.
Every later row is required to hold as many fields as there are names.
This is where a ragged file is refused rather than in `parse`: a name per
column is a promise that a row's third field is the third column, and a row
with a field missing quietly shifts every field after the gap.

entries.name: parseWith
doc: The same, for a text whose fields are separated by something else.
A tab is the other common answer, and a file that chose one is not
improved by a reader that assumes the other.

entries.name: record
doc: One row read by column name rather than by position.

entries.name: records
doc: Every row read by column name.

entries.name: render
doc: Rows written as comma-separated text, ending with a newline.

entries.name: renderTable
doc: A table written with its column names as the first row.

entries.name: renderWith
doc: The same, separated by something else.

entries.name: Table
doc: A table read with its first row taken as the names of its columns.

entries.name: affected
doc: How many rows a statement that produced none reported changing.
Read from the tag the server sends, which is the only place an update says
what it did. A caller checking that an update changed something is checking
this rather than a row count, which for an update is zero either way.

entries.name: asDriverRows
doc: This result as the driver layer carries one.
The session answers every column as text, because that is what the wire
carries; the driver layer carries what a value is. Converting here rather
than in each driver keeps one description of how a session's result becomes
a driver's, which two copies would eventually disagree about.

entries.name: begin
doc: Begin a transaction.

entries.name: beginWith
doc: Begin a transaction at a stated level of protection.

entries.name: closePool
doc: Close admission and every queued connection; borrowers close their own returns.

entries.name: column
doc: Every value in one column.

entries.name: Column
doc: A column of a result.

entries.name: commit
doc: Keep everything the transaction did.

entries.name: indexOfColumn
doc: Where a column sits, or `-1` when the result has no column of that name.

entries.name: inTransaction
doc: Whether a connection is inside a transaction, failed or not.

entries.name: Isolation
doc: How much a transaction is protected from what other transactions are doing.
Named rather than left to text, because these are the four the standard
defines and a caller writing one as a string can misspell it into whatever
the server's default happens to be — silently, since a server given an
unknown level reports nothing until it matters.

entries.name: pool
doc: A pool of open connections, shared between threads.
The connections are held in a channel, which is what makes taking one wait
rather than fail when they are all in use: a channel's receive already
blocks until something is there, so the pool needs no waiting of its own.
It also means a pool cannot hand out more connections than it opened, which
is the whole reason a database wants one.

entries.name: Pool
doc: A set of connections shared between threads.

entries.name: release
doc: Forget a marked point, keeping everything done since.

entries.name: rollback
doc: Undo everything the transaction did.
This is also how a connection whose transaction failed is made usable
again: the server refuses every other statement until it arrives.

entries.name: rollbackTo
doc: Undo back to a marked point, keeping what came before it.

entries.name: rowCount
doc: How many rows a result holds.

entries.name: Rows
doc: What a query produced.
A value that was absent is `None` rather than empty text, because the two
are different and a caller that could not tell them apart would read a
column nobody filled in as one somebody filled in with nothing.

entries.name: run
doc: Run a statement with values supplied apart from it.
The values never enter the text. The server plans the statement first and
is handed the values after, so a value holding a quotation mark, a
semicolon, or the whole of another statement is a value in a column and
cannot become part of what runs.

entries.name: savepoint
doc: Mark a point a transaction can be returned to without undoing all of it.

entries.name: simple
doc: Run text the server plans and executes in one step.
This cannot carry values, and nothing here will paste one into it. A query
built by joining text to a value is a query whose shape the value decides,
which is how a value becomes an instruction; `run` is the way to supply
one.

entries.name: statusOf
doc: Where a connection stands, so a caller can ask before acting.

entries.name: transaction
doc: Take a connection, run an action inside a transaction on it, and put it
back.
The connection is held for the whole operation, which is the point. A
caller that reaches for the pool once per statement gets a different
connection each time, so `BEGIN` lands on one and the work that was meant
to be inside it lands on another — and the transaction, holding nothing,
commits nothing and rolls back nothing. Nothing about that reads as wrong
at the call site; it appears as rows that should have been undone and were
not.
Holding one connection is also what stops another caller interleaving work
between the `BEGIN` and the `COMMIT`: a connection lent to this operation
is not in the pool for anyone else to take.

entries.name: transactionWith
doc: The same, at a stated level of protection.

entries.name: value
doc: One value by row and column name, absent when either is missing or when the
column had no value.

entries.name: withConnection
doc: Take a connection, hand it to an action, and put it back however the action
ended.
There is no return a caller can forget. A connection not put back is one
the pool has lost, and a pool that has lost all of them stops every thread
waiting on it — a failure that appears only under load and looks like the
database being slow.

entries.name: withSavepoint
entries.signature: Std.Db.Session.Connection -> Str -> fn(Std.Db.Session.Connection) -> (Result[T, Std.Db.Session.DbError], Std.Db.Session.Connection) -> (Result[T, Std.Db.Session.DbError], Std.Db.Session.Connection)
doc: Run an action between two marked points, undoing back to the first if it
failed.
The difference from a transaction is what a failure costs: this undoes only
what the action did, leaving the transaction around it intact, so one
optional step failing does not throw away the work before it.

entries.name: withTransaction
entries.signature: Std.Db.Session.Connection -> fn(Std.Db.Session.Connection) -> (Result[T, Std.Db.Session.DbError], Std.Db.Session.Connection) -> (Result[T, Std.Db.Session.DbError], Std.Db.Session.Connection)
doc: Run an action inside a transaction, and undo it if the action failed.
There is no rollback a caller can forget. A transaction left open holds
every row it touched against every other connection until something closes
it, and a caller that returned early on a failure — which is exactly when a
rollback matters most — is the commonest way one is left open.
A commit that itself fails is answered as a failure rather than swallowed:
a caller told its work was kept, when the server refused to keep it, would
carry on from a state that does not exist.

entries.name: connect
doc: Open a real PostgreSQL session from a connection URI.

entries.name: parse
doc: Parse connection settings without connecting or including secrets in errors.

entries.name: pool
doc: Open a bounded pool from a connection URI.

entries.name: ask
doc: Ask a transaction's own connection, rather than the pool.

entries.name: Client
doc: A driver owns synchronization and closes admission before releasing its resources.

entries.name: close
doc: Close a client and the connections it holds.

entries.name: Column
doc: A column in a result set: its name, and what the database calls its type.

entries.name: connect
doc: Open a client for a connection string, using the first driver that knows the scheme.

entries.name: Driver
doc: A connector is an ordinary value; applications choose which drivers they admit.

entries.name: error
doc: An error naming the driver, the kind of failure, and what happened.

entries.name: Error
doc: Why a database call did not succeed, and which driver said so.

entries.name: execute
doc: Run a statement that carries no values.

entries.name: Placeholders
doc: How a driver writes the places where values go in a statement.

entries.name: query
doc: Run a statement with values bound to its placeholders.

entries.name: Rows
doc: What a statement answered: its columns, its rows, and the command that ran.

entries.name: run
doc: Run a statement on the connection a transaction holds.

entries.name: select
doc: Select exactly one driver without exposing connection-string contents in errors.

entries.name: transaction
doc: Run an action inside a transaction, on one connection, whichever backend
this client is.

entries.name: Tx
doc: One connection, held for the length of a transaction.
Separate from `Client` because that is the whole difference: a client's
`query` reaches for whatever connection is free, and two of them in a row
need not be the same one. Everything asked of a `Tx` goes to the connection
the transaction is running on.

entries.name: Value
doc: Values retain their kind across the driver boundary; drivers bind them separately.

entries.name: Applied
doc: One that has already run, as the database records it.

entries.name: digestOf
doc: The digest of a migration's statements as they stand.
What makes an edit after the fact detectable. Without it, a database that
ran the old text and one that ran the new both report the same version, and
nothing afterwards can tell that their schemas differ.

entries.name: explain
doc: What a refusal says.

entries.name: migrate
doc: Bring the schema to what the program expects.
Each migration runs in its own transaction, so a failure leaves every
earlier one applied and the failing one absent and the record always
describes the schema. One transaction around all of them is attractive
until a statement that cannot run inside one appears.

entries.name: migration
doc: A migration from its parts.

entries.name: Migration
doc: One change to a schema.
A value, so the whole set a program holds can be listed, ordered, and
planned against a record without a database being present.

entries.name: MigrationError
doc: Why a schema will not be changed.

entries.name: ordered
doc: The migrations in version order, which is the order they are considered in.

entries.name: pendingCount
doc: How many migrations a plan would run.

entries.name: pendingVersions
doc: The versions a plan would run, in order.

entries.name: plan
doc: What should happen next, decided without a database.
A pure function of what the program holds and what the record reports, so
the decision is checked by comparing values and only carrying it out needs
a connection.

entries.name: Plan
doc: What should happen next.
Both halves are here rather than only the first: a caller that is about to
change a schema wants to see what is already there, and a report naming
only the pending ones cannot be checked against the record it came from.

entries.name: recordOf
doc: The record a database holds.
The table is made before it is read, because a first run against an empty
database is the ordinary case.

entries.name: settled
doc: Whether a plan has anything to do.

entries.name: connect
doc: Open a client on a PostgreSQL connection string.

entries.name: driver
doc: The PostgreSQL driver, for a set a program assembles itself.

entries.name: authenticationKind
doc: What kind of authentication the server asked for, read from the message
that asks.

entries.name: bind
doc: Values supplied for a planned statement's holes.
Every value is sent as text and every result asked for as text. That is the
slower of the two formats and the one whose meaning does not depend on the
server's word size or byte order, which is the right trade for a client
that must be correct against a server it did not build.
A value that is absent is sent as a length of minus one rather than as
empty, because the protocol distinguishes them and a column that is empty
is not a column that has nothing.

entries.name: bodyLength
doc: How many bytes a message needs beyond the five already read, or nothing
when the five are not yet there.
Separated from reading the message so a caller can ask for exactly what is
missing rather than reading a byte at a time.

entries.name: Column
doc: A column the server says a result will have.

entries.name: cString
doc: Text with the zero byte the protocol ends a string with.

entries.name: describeStatement
doc: Ask what shape a planned statement produces.

entries.name: execute
doc: Run a bound statement, with no limit on how many rows come back.

entries.name: fieldOf
doc: One field of an error, by the letter naming it.

entries.name: frame
doc: A message framed the way the protocol frames one: the letter, then the
length counting itself, then the payload.

entries.name: Message
doc: One message, as it travels: the letter naming its kind and the bytes after
the length.
The kind is kept as text rather than as a variant per message, because the
protocol has more kinds than any one client uses and a server is permitted
to send ones this client has never heard of. A variant per kind would make
an unknown message impossible to represent, and the only correct thing to
do with most of them is to read past them.

entries.name: messageSize
doc: Validate the length before a streaming reader allocates or requests a body.

entries.name: parse
doc: A statement given to the server to plan, with the values left as holes.

entries.name: password
doc: A password sent as the server asked for it.

entries.name: ProtocolError
doc: Why bytes on the wire did not make a message.

entries.name: query
doc: A simple query, which asks the server to plan and run text in one step.
This cannot carry parameters, and that is why `bind` exists: text with a
value pasted into it is a query whose shape depends on the value, which is
how a value becomes an instruction.

entries.name: readCString
doc: The text at the front of a payload, and what follows it.
A string with no terminator is a truncated message rather than a string
running to the end: reading it as one would let a message cut short look
like a complete one with a shorter field.

entries.name: readDataRow
doc: SQL NULL has one explicit sentinel; invalid or truncated text is not absent.

entries.name: readFields
doc: The fields an error or notice carries, keyed by the letter naming each.
Kept as the letters the protocol uses rather than as named fields, because
the set grows between server versions and a client that dropped what it did
not recognise would lose exactly the detail a new server added to help.

entries.name: readMessage
doc: Read one complete message, preserving any following frames.

entries.name: readRowDescription
doc: The columns a row description names.

entries.name: saslInitial
doc: The first message of a challenge, naming the mechanism and the opening
text.

entries.name: saslResponse
doc: A later message of a challenge, which carries only its text.

entries.name: startup
doc: The first message a connection sends, which carries no letter.
It is the one message framed without a kind, because the server does not
yet know what version is speaking to it and so cannot know how to read one.

entries.name: sync
doc: End the sequence, so the server reports and becomes ready again.
Without this the server holds everything sent since the last one, and a
client that never sends it waits for a reply that is waiting for it.

entries.name: terminate
doc: Say the connection is finished.

entries.name: VERSION
doc: The version this speaks: the third revision of the protocol, written as a
major and minor number packed into one word.

entries.name: absent
doc: A value that is absent.

entries.name: also
doc: A further condition that must also hold.

entries.name: andOn
doc: A further condition that must also hold.

entries.name: counting
doc: How many rows a table holds.

entries.name: deleteFrom
doc: Rows removed from a table.

entries.name: either
doc: A further condition where either may hold.

entries.name: empty
doc: A statement with nothing in it.

entries.name: except
doc: The rows in the first and not the second.

entries.name: explain
doc: What a refusal says.

entries.name: flag
doc: A value that is true or false.

entries.name: from
doc: Everything from a table.

entries.name: fromTable
doc: Everything from the table a column belongs to.
Taken from the column rather than written again, so the table a statement
reads and the columns it names cannot disagree.

entries.name: insert
doc: A row added to a table, from the columns and the values that fill them.

entries.name: intersect
doc: The rows in both.

entries.name: limit
doc: At most this many rows.
A number rather than a parameter, because it is written by the program and
a database plans better when it knows it. It is a whole number by its type,
so nothing else can arrive here.

entries.name: matching
doc: A condition on a column, with the value travelling beside the statement.

entries.name: matchingMissing
doc: A condition that a column holds nothing.

entries.name: matchingOneOf
doc: A condition that a column is one of several values.
Each value is its own parameter, so a list from outside cannot become part
of the text however long it is.

entries.name: maybeText
doc: Text, or its absence.

entries.name: missingOn
doc: A condition that a column holds nothing.

entries.name: name
doc: A name, admitted only when it is one.
A table or a column cannot be a parameter, which is why a name taken from
a request is an injection point that parameters do not close. Refused
rather than quoted: quoting correctly depends on the dialect, and a quoted
name that was wrong is an injection that looks handled.

entries.name: offset
doc: Starting after this many rows.

entries.name: on
doc: A condition on a column, with the column and the comparison both values.
This is the form worth using. The column is a name the compiler knows, so
the editor offers it and writing one that does not exist is refused where
it is written rather than when the statement runs. The value is checked
against what the column holds, so comparing text to a number does not
compile. And nothing here takes a name or an operator as text, so there is
no spelling for either to arrive wrong in.

entries.name: oneOf
doc: A name chosen from a list the program wrote.
What a program uses when a name really does come from outside: the choice
is between things the program named, so nothing outside decides anything.

entries.name: operator
doc: An operator, admitted only when it is one.

entries.name: orderBy
doc: The order rows come back in.

entries.name: orderOn
doc: The order rows come back in, by a column the compiler knows.

entries.name: orOn
doc: A further condition where either may hold.

entries.name: Part
doc: A statement, and the values that travel beside it.
The text is built only from parts the program wrote. Everything that came
from outside is in `values`, and there is no call that moves one into the
other — which is what makes an injection unrepresentable here rather than
prevented by a rule someone remembers at every call site.
One piece of a statement: text the program wrote, or the place a value goes.
A placeholder is a part rather than text reading `$3`, and that is what
makes joining two statements cost nothing. Written into the text, a
placeholder has to be found again and renumbered whenever a statement is
put after another — which means scanning every character of it, on every
join. Kept as a part, the numbers are never written until the text is
asked for, and then they are written once, in order.

entries.name: qualifiedName
doc: A name that may carry the table it belongs to.
Needed wherever a statement reaches more than one table: once a join is in
play, every condition names its column with the table, and a check that
admitted only a bare name would refuse every one of them. Each part is
checked separately rather than the whole against a looser rule, because a
rule loose enough to admit a dot is loose enough to admit what follows one.

entries.name: QueryError
doc: Why a statement would not be built.

entries.name: raw
doc: A statement written out in full, with its values beside it.
The way out. A builder that cannot express something forces a way around
it, and the way around should keep values apart rather than abandoning the
property the builder exists for — so this takes the text and the values
separately, exactly as everything else here does. Anything the language can
say goes through here: window functions, recursive traversal, a call to a
function the database defines, a statement somebody tuned by hand.
The placeholders written in the text are read and held as parts, so a
statement written this way can still be put after another one and have its
numbering come out right. Written as text and left alone, `$1` in the
second of two statements would still say `$1` after the first had already
used it.

entries.name: returning
doc: A statement that answers with the rows it changed.

entries.name: selecting
doc: Named columns from a table.

entries.name: Statement
doc: The parts are held rather than one text, because a statement is built a
clause at a time and appending to text copies everything built so far — so
a statement assembled from many pieces cost the square of its length. They
are joined once, when the text is asked for.
The values are typed, not text.
A comparison written against a number has to reach the backend as one. Bound
as text it is compared as text, and SQLite orders every number before every
text — so `sum(quantity) > '6'` is false for every row it could be asked
about, and the answer is an empty result rather than an error. PostgreSQL
coerces the text and answers correctly, so the same query means two things.
Carrying the type is what stops the builder deciding that by accident.

entries.name: Statement
doc: The parts are held rather than one text, because a statement is built a
clause at a time and appending to text copies everything built so far — so
a statement assembled from many pieces cost the square of its length. They
are joined once, when the text is asked for.
The values are typed, not text.
A comparison written against a number has to reach the backend as one. Bound
as text it is compared as text, and SQLite orders every number before every
text — so `sum(quantity) > '6'` is false for every row it could be asked
about, and the answer is an empty result rather than an error. PostgreSQL
coerces the text and answers correctly, so the same query means two things.
Carrying the type is what stops the builder deciding that by accident.

entries.name: text
doc: A statement from text the program wrote, carrying no values.
For the parts a builder does not cover. Values still travel separately —
there is no door here that takes them any other way.

entries.name: textIn
doc: The same statement, spelled the way one backend writes a placeholder.
PostgreSQL takes `$1`, SQLite takes `?` as well as `$1`, and a backend that
takes only `?` refuses the first. Which one a driver takes is already
declared on it, so a caller with a driver in hand can ask here rather than
writing a spelling by hand and finding out from the database which backends
it happened to suit.

entries.name: textOf
doc: The text a statement holds, which a program may read before running it.

entries.name: textValue
doc: A value that is text.

entries.name: textValuesOf
doc: The same values as the text a wire carries.
PostgreSQL's protocol sends every parameter as text, so a session speaks
this rather than the typed form. It is a rendering for one transport and not
a second opinion about what the values are: a number is written out here and
stays a number everywhere else.

entries.name: then
doc: Two statements one after the other, with the second's placeholders
renumbered to follow the first's.
Two statements one after the other.
Nothing is renumbered and nothing is scanned: the placeholders are parts,
so putting one statement after another is putting its parts after the
other's, and the numbers are written when the text is.

entries.name: union
doc: Two results together, with the second's values following the first's.

entries.name: update
doc: Columns of a table set to new values.
The conditions that choose which rows are added afterwards, so their
placeholders follow the ones the assignments used.

entries.name: valueCount
doc: How many values a statement carries.

entries.name: valuesOf
doc: The values that travel beside it.

entries.name: whole
doc: A value that is a whole number, so a numeric comparison is a numeric one.

entries.name: withQuery
doc: A named result the rest of a statement reads from.

entries.name: withValue
doc: A statement with one more piece of text and one more value.
The only way a value enters a statement. The placeholder is written here
rather than by the caller, so a caller cannot write one that does not
correspond to a value they supplied.

entries.name: ascending
doc: Rows ordered by a column, with the ones holding nothing last.

entries.name: Bound
doc: How much of a result is wanted. Nothing for either means all of it.

entries.name: Condition
doc: One condition, on a row or on a group.

entries.name: crossJoin
doc: Every row of one table beside every row of another.

entries.name: descending
doc: The same, largest first.

entries.name: everything
doc: Everything, which names nothing and so needs no checking.

entries.name: everythingFrom
doc: Everything from a table, which is the smallest query there is.

entries.name: first
doc: At most this many rows.

entries.name: fullJoin
doc: The same, keeping the rows of both that match nothing.

entries.name: howMany
doc: How many rows there are.

entries.name: inner
doc: A table joined where two columns agree.

entries.name: is
doc: A column compared against text, which travels as a parameter.
Text, and only text. A number written here is compared as text, and SQLite
orders every number before every text — so a bar written `is("total", ">",
"6")` is one no total clears, and the answer is an empty result rather than
an error. `isNumber` is what a numeric comparison is written with.

entries.name: isAmong
doc: The same, where each value carries its own type.

entries.name: isBound
doc: A column compared against a value that carries its own type.

entries.name: isMissing
doc: A column holding nothing.

entries.name: isNumber
doc: A column compared against a whole number, which crosses as one.

entries.name: isOneOf
doc: A column that is one of several values, each its own parameter, so a list
from outside cannot become part of the text however long it is.

entries.name: isPresent
doc: A column holding something.

entries.name: isValue
doc: The same, where the value may be absent.

entries.name: Join
doc: A table put beside the one a statement reads from.

entries.name: Joining
doc: How two tables are put beside one another.

entries.name: joinOn
doc: A join on two columns whose types must agree, so joining a column of text
to one of numbers does not compile.

entries.name: leftJoin
doc: The same, keeping rows of the first table that match nothing.

entries.name: Locking
doc: Whether the rows a statement reads are held for this transaction.

entries.name: ordered
doc: The same, saying where the rows holding nothing go.
Stated rather than left to the server's default, because that default
differs by direction and a page that reorders itself when a column becomes
nullable is a bug nobody looks for.

entries.name: Ordering
doc: One column a result is ordered by, and where the rows holding nothing go.

entries.name: over
doc: An aggregate over a column.

entries.name: page
doc: One page of a result.

entries.name: pick
doc: A column a statement answers with.

entries.name: qualifiedName
doc: A name that may carry the table it belongs to.

entries.name: Refining
doc: A query with one part changed, each answering the query rather than taking
it apart.
Written as methods so that a query built a clause at a time reads down the
page. As functions taking the query first, changing several things meant
wrapping each call in the next, and the result read inside out: the table
and the columns — the two things a reader looks for first — ended up
furthest in, and the shape on the page was the shape of the nesting rather
than the shape of the query. A method chain puts the clauses in the order
they are thought of, and the whole `Select` record stays available for the
queries a program knows in full.
Each answers a new query and leaves the one it was asked of alone, which is
what makes adding a clause in a loop safe: a search screen adds a filter for
each thing the reader typed and nothing else about the query moves.

entries.name: rightJoin
doc: The same, the other way about.

entries.name: select
doc: A whole query as a statement, or the first thing wrong with it.
The clauses are written in the order the language reads them, so what is
built is what runs rather than something a server has to be lenient about.
Everything that could be a name is checked here, in one place, rather than
at each of the calls that put the query together.

entries.name: Select
doc: A whole query, written as one value.
Every part is visible at once, which is the point. A query assembled by
calls that each take the last one reads inside out: the thing a reader
wants first — what it reads from and what it answers with — ends up
furthest in, and the shape of the query is the shape of the nesting rather
than anything about the query. Written this way it reads in the order it is
thought of, and the parts a query does not need are empty rather than
absent.

entries.name: Selected
doc: One thing a statement answers with.

entries.name: selectedText
doc: How one of them is written.

entries.name: Test
doc: What a condition asks.

entries.name: unbounded
doc: All of a result.

entries.name: under
doc: The same thing, answering under a name of its own.

entries.name: all
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> Result[Array[T], Std.Db.Repository.RowError]
doc: Every row as a value.
The first failure stops it, because a partial list of what a query returned
is a value a caller cannot act on and cannot tell from a complete one.

entries.name: changed
doc: How many rows a statement that produced none reported changing.

entries.name: column
doc: One column of every row, mapped.

entries.name: count
doc: One column as a count, which may not.

entries.name: explain
doc: What a refusal says.

entries.name: first
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> Result[Option[T], Std.Db.Repository.RowError]
doc: The first row as a value, for a caller that asked for several and means it.

entries.name: hasColumn
doc: Whether a result has a column of that name.
Asked before reading, because the layer beneath cannot tell a column that
is not there from one that held nothing, and inheriting that turns a typo
into a data condition found later and somewhere else.

entries.name: Mapper
doc: How a row becomes a value.
A pure function of a result and a row number, so a program's mapping is
checked by building a result and comparing values. Mapping is where the
errors are, and a database is the slowest way to find them.

entries.name: nameOf
doc: What the repository is over.

entries.name: one
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> Result[T, Std.Db.Repository.RowError]
doc: Exactly one row as a value.
A lookup that found none and one that found several are different, and both
are refused. Answering the first of several is how a program acts on the
wrong record without anything appearing to go wrong.

entries.name: optional
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> Result[Option[T], Std.Db.Repository.RowError]
doc: At most one row as a value.
For a lookup by something unique, where finding nothing is an ordinary
answer and finding several is still a fault.

entries.name: optionalText
doc: One column of one row as text, which must be there and may hold nothing.

entries.name: repository
entries.signature: Str -> fn(K) -> Result[Option[T], Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> fn() -> Result[Array[T], Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> fn(T) -> Result[Int, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> fn(K) -> Result[Int, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> Std.Db.Repository.Repository[T, K]
doc: A repository from its operations.

entries.name: Repository
doc: What a program can do with one kind of thing.
A record of functions. Nothing here proxies an interface into an
implementation or derives a statement from a name — what a repository does
is what somebody wrote in it, which also means a repository over a
different backing is the same record with different functions.

entries.name: RowError
doc: Why a row would not become a value.
The column is named and the value is not. The value came from the database
and may be anything, and a message is a place values end up rendered; the
column is what a caller acts on.

entries.name: text
doc: One column of one row as text, which must be there and must hold something.

entries.name: truth
doc: One column as a truth.
The spellings accepted are the ones a database sends. Anything else is
refused rather than read as false, because a column that silently means the
opposite of what it holds is worse than one that stops the program.

entries.name: whole
doc: One column as a whole number, which may be below nothing.
Taken from the value the backend already decoded where it decoded one,
rather than read back out of its digits.

entries.name: wholeOr
doc: One column as a whole number, or a fallback when it holds nothing.

entries.name: at
doc: The value at a row and column, both counted from zero.

entries.name: bytes
doc: A named column read as raw bytes.

entries.name: decimal
doc: A named column read as an exact decimal.

entries.name: indexOf
doc: Named access refuses duplicate labels, which require aliases or indexed access.

entries.name: integer
doc: A named column read as a whole number.

entries.name: map
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Row.RowError] -> Result[Array[T], Std.Db.Row.RowError]
doc: Mapping order follows the result; the first mapper failure stops consumption.

entries.name: Mapper
doc: Turns one row into a value, or says why it could not.

entries.name: nullable
doc: None means a present SQL NULL, never a missing column or malformed row.

entries.name: one
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Row.RowError] -> Result[T, Std.Db.Row.RowError]
doc: The single row a query answered, or an error when it answered none or several.

entries.name: optional
entries.signature: &Std.Db.Driver.Rows -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Row.RowError] -> Result[Option[T], Std.Db.Row.RowError]
doc: The one row a query answered, or nothing. Several rows is an error.

entries.name: real
doc: A named column read as a binary floating number.

entries.name: RowError
doc: Why a value could not be read out of a result set.

entries.name: text
doc: A named column read as text. A null is an error, not an empty string.

entries.name: truth
doc: A named column read as a truth value.

entries.name: value
doc: The value in a named column of a row, whatever its kind.

entries.name: Bindable
doc: How a value is written when it travels as a parameter.
Separate from how a value is shown to a person, because showing text quotes
it and a quoted value in a parameter is a different value. That mistake
passes every test written with numbers.
A value carries its own type across, rather than its spelling.
Rendering a number to text here is what makes a numeric comparison a text
one at the far end. SQLite orders every number before every text, so a bar
bound as text is a bar no number clears, and the answer is an empty result
rather than an error.

entries.name: boundValue
doc: A value as the parameter it becomes.

entries.name: column
doc: A column of a table.
Declared once, in a module that stands for the table, so every query names
it through that module — which is what makes the editor offer it and a
wrong name refuse to compile.

entries.name: Column
doc: A column: where it lives, what it is called, and what it holds.
The type parameter is what makes comparing a column of text against a
number fail to compile rather than reach the database.

entries.name: Comparison
doc: The comparisons a condition may use.
Values rather than text, so the editor offers them and a misspelling is a
compile error rather than something to check for at run time.

entries.name: comparisonText
doc: How a comparison is written.

entries.name: nameOf
doc: What a column is called.

entries.name: namesOf
doc: The names of several columns, for the places a statement lists them.

entries.name: nothing
doc: Nothing, for a column that is being set to hold nothing.

entries.name: qualified
doc: The column named with its table, for a statement over more than one.

entries.name: tableOf
doc: Which table it belongs to.

entries.name: at
doc: The same, somewhere else.

entries.name: close
doc: Say the connection is finished, and close it.

entries.name: config
doc: A configuration pointing at a database on this machine.

entries.name: Config
doc: Where a database is and who is asking.

entries.name: connect
doc: Open a connection and take it through to the point it will accept a query.

entries.name: Connection
doc: A connection, and the bytes read from it that have not yet made a message.
The connection is threaded rather than held, like a random generator: every
operation answers the connection to use next. The alternative is a value
that changes when it is read, which is the one thing no other value in the
language does.

entries.name: DbError
doc: Opening a connection and keeping it: the handshake, what the server asks
for, and the messages that cross afterwards.
Separated from [[Std Db]] because the two answer different questions. This
one knows how to become a connection and how to read one message; that one
knows what a query is, what a transaction promises, and how a pool hands a
connection round. Authentication in particular is where a mistake is
quietest, and it is easier to read when it is not surrounded by row access.
Why a database operation did not do what it was asked.
A failure the server reported is kept apart from every other kind, and
carries the code the server gave it. That code is what a caller acts on: a
unique-key violation is retried differently from a syntax error, and a
caller matching on the text of a message would break when the server was
translated or upgraded.

entries.name: DEFAULT_MESSAGE_BYTES
doc: Complete tagged-message budget, including the tag and four-byte length word.

entries.name: emptyMessage
doc: A message carrying nothing, for a read that found none.

entries.name: live
doc: Whether this value still names the current lending of its connection.
Checked where a statement is written rather than where a connection is
passed, because writing is the point at which a stale copy would put bytes
into a conversation that is no longer its own.

entries.name: nextMessage
doc: Read the next message, taking more from the socket only when what has
arrived does not already hold one.
Reading a message at a time from the socket directly would ask for its five
byte head and then its body as two reads, and a server is free to send
several messages in one packet. Buffering is what makes the reader agree
with what the server actually sends rather than with how it was drawn.

entries.name: nextMessageLimited
doc: Read one bounded message. A broken or partially consumed transport is closed.

entries.name: renew
doc: End this lending and begin the next one.
The returned value is the connection under its new lending; every copy
handed out under the old one stops working. The connection itself is
untouched — it is the right to use it that moved.

entries.name: serverFailure
doc: The failure a server-reported error carries.

entries.name: TransactionStatus
doc: Where a connection stands with respect to a transaction.
The server reports this with every message saying it is ready, and it is
worth keeping rather than inferring: after a statement fails inside a
transaction the server refuses everything until the transaction is rolled
back, so a caller that assumed it was still usable would see every later
statement fail for a reason that has nothing to do with it.

entries.name: withStatus
doc: The transaction status the server reports with every message saying it is
ready: idle, inside a transaction, or inside one that has failed.

entries.name: write
doc: Send bytes to the server.

entries.name: connect
doc: One serialized connection preserves a single database for :memory: clients.

entries.name: driver
doc: The SQLite driver, for a set a program assembles itself.

entries.name: belongingTo
doc: What belongs to one parent, out of what was loaded for many.

entries.name: change
entries.signature: Std.Db.Session.Connection -> &Std.Db.Store.Stored[T] -> Option[Str] -> T -> Result[(Int, Std.Db.Session.Connection), Std.Db.Store.StoreError]
doc: Change the one a key names.

entries.name: deleteOf
doc: The statement that removes the one a key names.

entries.name: explain
doc: What a refusal says.

entries.name: forParent
doc: What belongs to one parent, which is what belongs to a list of one.

entries.name: forParents
doc: The statement that reads everything belonging to any of these parents.
One statement for every parent rather than one for each, with each key its
own parameter so a list of parents cannot become part of the text however
long it is.

entries.name: groupedBy
doc: What belongs to several parents, as a map from each parent's key to what
belongs to it.
This is the shape that matters. Loading what belongs to one parent is
loading for a list of one, so the batched form is the ordinary form and the
form that issues a query per parent is the one somebody has to write a loop
to produce. Offering both as peers is how the slow one becomes the default.

entries.name: insertOf
doc: The statement that adds one.

entries.name: keyOf
doc: Which column identifies one.

entries.name: keysOf
doc: The keys of several parents, for the statement that loads their children.

entries.name: load
doc: Read the one a key names.

entries.name: loadAll
doc: Read every one.

entries.name: loadForParents
entries.signature: Std.Db.Session.Connection -> &Std.Db.Store.Stored[T] -> Str -> &Array[Option[Str]] -> Result[(Map[Str, Array[T]], Std.Db.Session.Connection), Std.Db.Store.StoreError]
doc: Read everything belonging to any of these parents, in one statement.

entries.name: loadWhere
doc: Read everything a statement chooses.

entries.name: readAll
doc: Every row of a result as a value.

entries.name: readOne
doc: At most one row of a result as a value.

entries.name: remove
doc: Remove the one a key names.

entries.name: save
doc: Add one, and say how many rows it changed.

entries.name: selectAllOf
doc: The statement that reads every one.

entries.name: selectOf
doc: The statement that reads the one a key names.

entries.name: stored
entries.signature: Str -> Str -> &Array[Str] -> fn(T) -> Array[Option[Str]] -> fn(Std.Db.Driver.Rows, Int) -> Result[T, Std.Db.Repository.RowError] -> Std.Db.Store.Stored[T]
doc: Describe how a value is written to a table and read back.

entries.name: Stored
doc: How a kind of value is kept.
Both directions are stated and neither is derived: a row becomes a value by
a function somebody wrote, and a value becomes a row the same way. Nothing
reads a shape to guess a column, so renaming a field is not a silent change
to a schema, and the mapping is checked by comparing values with no
database present.

entries.name: StoreError
doc: Why a value would not be kept or read back.

entries.name: tableOf
doc: Which table a kind of value lives in.

entries.name: updateOf
doc: The statement that changes the one a key names.

entries.name: abs
doc: The value with its sign removed.

entries.name: ceiling
doc: The smallest whole value at or above this one.

entries.name: defaultRounding
doc: The mode to reach for when nothing else is stated.
Half-even is the mode that does not accumulate bias across many roundings,
which is the whole reason a total computed one way matches the same total
computed another way.

entries.name: divide
doc: Divide to a stated number of fractional digits, rounding as told.
This is the operation to reach for when `left / right` reports that the
exact quotient does not terminate. It answers `None` only for a divisor of
nought, because the caller has already said what to do about a quotient
that runs on.

entries.name: divideHalfEven
doc: Divide half-even to a stated number of fractional digits.

entries.name: floor
doc: The largest whole value at or below this one.

entries.name: fromInt
doc: The decimal a whole number names. Every integer is exactly representable,
so this cannot fail.

entries.name: isNegative
doc: Whether a value is below nought.

entries.name: isZero
doc: Whether a value is nought, whatever scale it carries.

entries.name: max
doc: Which of two values is larger.

entries.name: mean
doc: The mean of an array to a stated number of digits, `None` when it is empty.

entries.name: min
doc: Which of two values is smaller.

entries.name: negate
doc: The value with its sign flipped.

entries.name: one
doc: One.

entries.name: parse
doc: Read a decimal from text, answering `None` when the text is not one.
There is deliberately no conversion from `Float64`. A binary float that
prints as `0.1` is not the number `0.1`, and letting it become `0.1d`
silently would import exactly the error this type exists to avoid.

entries.name: parseOr
doc: Read a decimal from text, falling back when the text is not one.

entries.name: percentOf
doc: A percentage of a value, to a stated number of digits.

entries.name: product
doc: The product of an array, one when it is empty.

entries.name: rescale
doc: Give a value a stated scale, rounding half-even if digits must be dropped.
This is what a monetary amount is normalised through: `rescale(total, 2)`
says the answer is in cents and means it.

entries.name: round
doc: Round to a number of fractional digits.
Asking for more digits than the value carries is exact: the value is
rescaled and nothing is decided. Asking for fewer is where the mode acts.

entries.name: roundHalfEven
doc: Round half-even to a number of fractional digits.

entries.name: Rounding
doc: How to decide a digit that does not fit.
All seven modes every base-ten standard converges on. Offering a subset
would only push programs into writing worse versions of the missing ones.

entries.name: scale
doc: How many fractional digits a value carries.
This is the one place a trailing zero is visible: `scale(1.50d)` is 2 and
`scale(1.5d)` is 1, even though the two compare equal.

entries.name: signum
doc: `-1`, `0`, or `1` as the value is below, at, or above nought.

entries.name: sum
doc: The sum of an array, nought when it is empty.

entries.name: toFloat64
doc: The nearest binary floating value.
Lossy in both the ways it can be: a coefficient may carry more significant
digits than `Float64` holds, and a terminating base-ten fraction is usually
not one in base two. Use it to hand a number to something that needs a
float, never to compute with.

entries.name: toInt
doc: The whole number a decimal names, when it names one exactly.
Answers `None` for a value with a fractional part.

entries.name: toText
doc: The text a decimal renders as, keeping exactly the fractional digits its
scale claims.

entries.name: truncate
doc: Round to a whole number, keeping the decimal type.

entries.name: zero
doc: Nought.

entries.name: back
doc: The element at the back, or `None` for an empty queue.

entries.name: concat
doc: Two queues joined, the left one's elements first.

entries.name: contains
doc: Whether an element is present.

entries.name: Deque
doc: A queue that can be added to and taken from at either end.
An array is cheap at its back and dear at its front: adding or removing a
first element moves every other one. A program that queues work — a
breadth-first walk, a scheduler, a window over a stream — takes from the
front on every step, and pays that cost on every step.
This holds two arrays instead. The front is kept reversed, so taking from
the front and adding to the back are both work at the end of an array,
which is where an array is cheap. When one side runs out, the other is
split across the two. Each element moves a bounded number of times over its
life in the queue, so the cost per operation averages out to a constant
even though a single one occasionally does more.

entries.name: dropBack
doc: The queue without its back element, unchanged when there is none.

entries.name: dropFront
doc: The queue without its front element, unchanged when there is none.

entries.name: empty
doc: A queue with nothing in it.

entries.name: filter
doc: The elements that satisfy a test, order kept.

entries.name: fold
doc: The elements combined from the front.

entries.name: fromArray
doc: A queue holding the elements of an array, first at the front.

entries.name: front
doc: The element at the front, or `None` for an empty queue.

entries.name: get
doc: The element at a position counted from the front, or `None`.

entries.name: isEmpty
doc: Whether the queue holds nothing.

entries.name: length
doc: How many elements the queue holds.

entries.name: map
doc: Every element transformed, order kept.

entries.name: popBack
doc: The back element and the queue without it, or `None` when there is none.

entries.name: popFront
doc: The front element and the queue without it, or `None` when there is none.
Both are answered together because a caller almost always wants both, and
asking twice would walk the same rebalancing twice.

entries.name: pushBack
doc: The queue with an element added at the back.

entries.name: pushFront
doc: The queue with an element added at the front.

entries.name: reversed
doc: The queue with its ends exchanged, so what was first is last.

entries.name: toArray
doc: Every element in order, front first.

entries.name: DiffHunk
doc: Grouped unified diff hunk.

entries.name: diffLines
doc: Computes the minimal edit script transforming lines of oldText to newText.

entries.name: DiffOp
doc: Elementary edit script operation.

entries.name: diffTokens
doc: Computes the minimal edit script across token sequences using Myers O(ND) algorithm.

entries.name: levenshtein
doc: Computes the minimum number of edits to transform s1 into s2.

entries.name: similarity
doc: Normalized similarity score from 0.0 (disjoint) to 1.0 (identical).

entries.name: unifiedDiff
entries.signature: Str -> Str -> Str -> Str -> Int -> Str
doc: Formats sequence differences in standard Unified Diff format.

entries.name: componentCount
doc: Returns the number of disconnected components remaining.

entries.name: componentSize
doc: Returns the number of elements in the component containing `x`.

entries.name: connected
doc: Tests whether elements `x` and `y` belong to the same component.
